subject: SUBTRACT statement
notes: kb/Work/PB392.md LANDED - all THREE divergences this row recorded are closed and the rule is now asked as the SET it names. RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.44.3 'Identifier-4 and identifier-5 shall be alphanumeric group items, national group items, variable-length groups, or strongly-typed group items and shall not be described with level-number 66.' -> OK, 14.9.44.3 6). (1) The VARIABLE-LENGTH-GROUP leg closed with kb/Work PB393 (CorrAccess.Create switches on Place.Undecorated), re-measured here: two occurs-depending groups give P=0007. (2) The elementary-operand and level-66 legs closed with kb/Work PB390 (the screen moved into StatementValidation and reports at BIND time naming SR6). (3) THE BIT-GROUP LEG IS THIS LANDING. The screen read the boolean DataItem.IsGroup where SR6 names FOUR of the five group kinds, so a GROUP-USAGE BIT group was ADMITTED and the statement then ran as a silent no-op - 3.11 defines an alphanumeric group item as a 'group item except for a bit group item, a national group item, a strongly-typed group item, or a variable-length group item', so a bit group is in none of SR6's four, and 14.7.6 rule 3 ('In an ADD or SUBTRACT statement, both of the data items are numeric data items') is why the rule leaves it out: 13.18.29.4 GR1 b) makes a bit group 'an elementary data item of usage bit and class and category boolean', so no implied pair could ever correspond. MEASURED BEFORE at --std 2023: SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING SRC FROM DST over two GROUP-USAGE BIT groups compiled, ran, printed OK and changed nothing. AFTER: two COBOL1757 diagnostics (both operands are screened before the verdict), 'SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING operand SRC is a bit group item (ISO 13.18.29.4 GR1) - the operands shall be alphanumeric group items, national group items, variable-length groups, or strongly-typed group items (ISO 14.9.44.3 SR6)'. THE SHAPE: ItemCategory.GroupKindsOf is the ONE reader of which of the five kinds an item IS, as a [Flags] SET - 13.18.29.3 SR1 ('The GROUP-USAGE clause may be specified only if the subject of the entry is a group item that is not strongly typed and not a variable-length group') keeps bit and national disjoint from the other two and 3.11 makes alphanumeric the complement, but nothing keeps STRONGLY-TYPED and VARIABLE-LENGTH apart, so a scalar enum would answer a rule admitting only one of them wrongly. Each verb's admitted set is a CorrespondingOperandRule ROW (clause + kinds + whether its text names level-66), and the diagnostic's admitted-set phrase is generated from the set by ItemCategory.Spell so the message cannot disagree with the check. The admitted kinds are pinned positively by conformance:cases/14.9.2-ADD/pb392_corresponding_group_kinds (an alphanumeric-group and a national-group SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING, values computed from 14.9.44.4 GR5 and 14.6.10 GR3: 3-10 stored as 007, 2-7 as 005).
